title: Add Geographic Chart Mark

complexity.rationale: Vega has first-class support for geo projections and geoshape/geopoint marks, so the basemap + point-projection rendering itself is a well-documented, native capability, not custom geometry. The genuinely new pieces are: lazy-loading a TopoJSON world-atlas asset (a bundling/code-splitting concern with no existing data-asset precedent in this codebase, distinct from the component-level lazy() splitting used elsewhere), click-to-zoom-to-a-point animating the projection's scale/translate (a new but well-understood signal-expression technique), zoom/pan (reusing add-network-mark's shared infra if available), and a region-fill (choropleth) mode joining data to basemap features by region id — also a native Vega pattern (`lookup` transform + `geoshape`), not new geometry. Each is bounded in scope with no deep open unknowns.

summary: A geographic mark using a natural-earth geo projection over a lazy-loaded world-atlas TopoJSON basemap, with zoom/pan and click-to-zoom-to-point. Supports two modes: point map (`latitude`/`longitude` per row) and region-fill/choropleth (a region identifier joined to basemap features, colored by value).
requirements: Point-map mode: accepts `latitude`, `longitude` (required) and an optional `label` channel; each row renders as a point on the map

Region-fill (choropleth) mode: accepts a `region` identifier (matching a basemap feature id at a configurable granularity — country/state/etc.) and a `value` field, coloring each matched region via a sequential color scale instead of plotting points
Renders a world basemap from a lazily-loaded TopoJSON asset (not bundled eagerly with the mark) under a natural-earth (or equivalent) geo projection
Supports zoom and pan over the map
In point-map mode, clicking a point animates the projection to center and zoom in 4x on that point
Supports region drill-down in choropleth mode (clicking a region can re-scope to a finer-grained basemap for that region, e.g. country to state)

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Render the existing EmptyState (basemap may still render, or be suppressed — needs a decision, see openQuestions).
Excluded from the point layer (off-map coordinates should not throw a projection error or render at an undefined position).

edgeCases.case: Two points at nearly identical coordinates
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Both render, potentially overlapping — no automatic clustering/jitter in this spec.

edgeCases.case: Clicking a point while already zoomed into a different point
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Re-centers and re-zooms to the newly clicked point from the current zoom state, rather than requiring a manual zoom-out first.
Render the point layer without a basemap (or an explicit error state) rather than leaving the whole mark blank — needs a decision on which fallback.

edgeCases.case: Choropleth mode: a region id with no matching basemap feature
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: That row is excluded from the fill join rather than throwing on a failed lookup.

edgeCases.case: Choropleth mode: a basemap feature with no matching data row
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Renders with a neutral/unfilled default color rather than an undefined or transparent fill.
Basemap and point colors resolve through the existing colorScheme-aware color scale / theme-aware landmass fill.
S1-only for this spec; no S2 port until the mark stabilizes out of rc status.
Projection scale/translate recompute against container size via the existing responsive sizing hook.

crossCutting.notes: touchesTooltipOrPopover: points/regions support ChartTooltip/ChartPopover, reusing existing interactive-mark plumbing. requiresNewSignalOrScale: true — reuses (or, if not yet built, duplicates) add-network-mark's zoomPanUtils.ts zoom/pan signals, a new click-to-zoom signal pair animating the Vega projection's scale/translate/center properties (a new signal target not used by any existing mark), a region-drill signal for choropleth mode, and add-heatmap-mark's sequential color scale for choropleth fill values. requiresS1S2Parity: false because this ships as a new s1-only rc-status mark, matching the Donut/BigNumber precedent; revisit once promoted out of rc.

implementationPlan.change: Create GeographicOptions/GeographicOptionsWithDefaults/GeographicSpecOptions with a `mode: 'point' | 'choropleth'` discriminant, point-mode `latitude`/`longitude`/`label` fields, and choropleth-mode `region`/`value` fields.
Add GeographicOptions to the MarkOptions union.
Fully-populated defaultGeographicOptions fixture, including an out-of-range-coordinate variant.

addTopoJsonBasemapData (lazy-loaded world-atlas source registration + `feature`/`mesh` transforms), addGeoPointTransform (Vega `geopoint` transform projecting latitude/longitude to x/y under the chosen projection, point mode), addChoroplethLookupTransform (Vega `lookup` transform joining `region` values onto basemap features by id, choropleth mode) — new to this codebase, though all use native Vega geo/lookup transforms rather than custom math.

getBasemapMark (geoshape mark for landmass, plain fill in point mode), getGeographicPointMark (symbol per data point at projected x/y, point mode), getChoroplethRegionMark (geoshape mark colored via a sequential scale off the joined value, choropleth mode, reusing add-heatmap-mark's addSequentialColorScale).

addGeographic, addData (branches on `mode`: calls addTopoJsonBasemapData + addGeoPointTransform for point mode, or addTopoJsonBasemapData + addChoroplethLookupTransform for choropleth mode), addSignals (click-to-zoom projection signals in point mode, a region-drill signal in choropleth mode, plus zoom/pan signals reusing marks/zoomPanUtils.ts from add-network-mark if it exists by implementation time, plus interactive-mark signals), setScales/projection (natural-earth projection object with signal-bound scale/translate/center, plus the sequential color scale in choropleth mode).
Unit tests for addTopoJsonBasemapData, addGeoPointTransform, and addChoroplethLookupTransform, including the invalid-coordinate and unmatched-region-id cases.
Unit tests for getBasemapMark/getGeographicPointMark/getChoroplethRegionMark using the fixture.
Per-function tests for addData/addSignals/setScales, including the click-to-zoom signal behavior.
Register geographicCount: -1 in initializeComponentCounts, import addGeographic, add the 'geographic' switch case.
GeographicProps/GeographicElement, Omit-ing only fields replaced at the React boundary (ChartTooltip/ChartPopover children).
Render-null component holding prop defaults, placed under rc/ per the Donut/BigNumber rc-status precedent.
Import Geographic from '../rc' and add its displayName dispatch case.
Add Geographic to the sanitizeRscChartChildren import/list from '../rc'.
Update the toStrictEqual ChartOptions snapshot to include the new mark type at default values.
Basic story plus a ClickToZoom interaction story.

openQuestions: Where does the TopoJSON world-atlas asset ship from — bundled in the package (bundle-size impact) or fetched from a CDN at runtime (network dependency, CSP implications given ast: true / credentials: 'omit' conventions used elsewhere)?
Should the basemap render (with no points/regions) or be suppressed entirely when data is empty?
Exact fallback behavior if the basemap asset fails to load.

What region granularities does choropleth mode need to support (country only, or country/state/city with drill-down between them), and does that require multiple TopoJSON assets loaded on demand per granularity?
